subject: Proposal: reserve-to-scale transition plan for Q1 peak (monthly commit uplift)
messages:
From: Alex Sullivan <alex.sullivan@fathomretail.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-28T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Q1 peak — looking to reserve more hosted capacity

Irene,

Thanks again for the overview earlier. Our engineering roadmap just landed — we have a confirmed marketing push in January that will likely triple inference volume for a 6-8 week window. We need to lock in additional committed capacity to avoid throttles and protect latency for customers.

Can you send a quick proposal for a short-term uplift (Nov–Mar) and an option to convert to a permanently higher monthly commit after the peak? Two priorities for us: predictable unit pricing during the peak and a burst cushion for the first two weeks of the campaign.

Also looping in procurement for any contracting logistics: procurement@fathomretail.com.

Thanks,
Alex Sullivan
Head of Product
Fathom Retail

--
Attachment: campaign_plan_Q1.xlsx (attachment stub)

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Sullivan <alex.sullivan@fathomretail.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-28T12:31:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Q1 peak — looking to reserve more hosted capacity

Alex — thanks for the heads up and congrats on the campaign. Sent a short proposal below that balances predictability during peak with a smooth path to a larger committed tier if you want to make the change permanent.

Summary proposal (high level):
- Short-term uplift: bump monthly committed tokens by 3x for Nov–Mar; pro-rated first invoice for Nov.
- Burst pocket: one-time 2x burst credit for the first 14 days (applies automatically, no additional sign-up).
- Transition clause: if Fathom converts to a permanent commit within 60 days after peak, the uplifted months count toward the annualized commit and we offer a 5% step discount on unit price for the converted portion.
- SLAs: keep existing latency SLOs; add a reserved throughput lane during campaign hours (9am–11pm PT) to protect tail latency.

Deliverables in next 48h: formal SOW + commit amendment + pricing sheet.
Questions for procurement (quick):
1) Does Fathom need vendor PO before DocuSign?
2) Any standard redlines we should expect on the amendment?

Next steps: if this shape looks right, I’ll draft the amendment and SOW and loop legal/finance for a short review. Karthik — can you sanity-check the price bands and burst calculation below and confirm we can honor the reserved lane in west-us-2?

Pricing sketch (example):
- Base monthly commit (existing): 2M tokens/mo — $X per 1K tokens
- Peak uplift monthly commit: 6M tokens/mo (Nov–Mar) — step unit price reduced by 4% versus base
- Burst cushion: 2x one-time credits usable during first 14 days

Regards,
Irene Choi
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

--
Attachments: pricing_sheet.csv (attached)

From: procurement@fathomretail.com
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Alex Sullivan <alex.sullivan@fathomretail.com>
Date: 2026-10-30T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Q1 peak — looking to reserve more hosted capacity

Hi Irene — procurement here. A few quick items so we can prep a PO and accelerate legal review:

1) Term and billing cadence: We prefer a single consolidated invoice monthly; if you propose a prorated November invoice, please include net-30 payment terms.
2) Data residency: confirm that logs and billing metadata for Fathom will remain in us-west region (we have compliance constraints).
3) Insurance and SOC2: please provide certificate references (SOC 2 Type II) and current insurance limits for vendor onboarding.
4) Contract redlines: we typically push back on automatic renewals and prefer a 30-day termination window for short-term promotions; is that acceptable for the uplift period?

We can expedite if you send the SOW + amendment and a DocuSign link.

Procurement Team
Fathom Retail

--
Attachment: onboarding_checklist.pdf (attachment stub)

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Sullivan <alex.sullivan@fathomretail.com>, procurement@fathomretail.com
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-03T15:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Q1 peak — looking to reserve more hosted capacity

Thanks — answers inline and next-step artifacts attached.

1) Billing cadence & payment terms: We will issue a prorated invoice for November and then monthly consolidated invoices thereafter; net-30 is fine.
2) Data residency: confirmed — logs and billing metadata for this contract will be stored and processed in us-west-2. I included a short note from our security team in the SOW.
3) SOC2 & insurance: see SOW (page 3) with SOC 2 Type II attestation link and cert reference; insurance limits summarized in the amendment.
4) Auto-renewal and termination: we can treat the uplift as a time-bound amendment (Nov 1–Mar 31). If Fathom opts into permanent commit conversion, we’ll attach the conversion language; otherwise the amendment expires at campaign end. For the uplift only: 30-day termination right is acceptable.

Attached: SOW_Fathom_Q1_peak.pdf, Commit_Amendment_v1.docx (redlines included), pricing_sheet.csv
DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/placeholder/12345
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/4859

Karthik — legal/finance asked you to confirm reserved lane capacity and that we can schedule a quick ops handoff (30 minutes) with Fathom's SRE before Jan 5 to lock in the throughput lane. Marissa — confirming you’re ok with the 5% conversion incentive on permanent commit.

If okay, I’ll send the DocuSign envelope for procurement and schedule the ops handoff.

Best,
Irene Choi
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

--
Attachments: SOW_Fathom_Q1_peak.pdf; Commit_Amendment_v1.docx; pricing_sheet.csv
